_note: Hand-annotated point pairs on open-licensed illusion photos (Wikimedia Commons). Coordinates are fractions of image width/height. Only pairs whose physical answer follows from geometry that is certain (hollow = concave, flat painted ground, Ames-room layout) are included. 'truth' is the point that is physically closer to the camera.

pairs.why: Ames room: the person who looks smaller stands in the far corner of a trapezoidal room; her feet are also higher in the image on a floor built to look level.
Same two people, points on their legs: the left person is in the near corner.
Concave mask: the nose tip lies behind the board surface; the board point is on the side nearer the camera.
Concave mask: the eye region is recessed behind the board; the board point is on the near side.
Hollow faces at Puzzling World: the nose is recessed into the panel, the panel corner is on the panel surface.
Hollow face (row 3): nose recessed behind the panel surface.
The parrots are paint on flat ground: the parrot head is higher in the image than the asphalt point, so on a flat ground it is farther.
The boot is paint on flat paving: its 'top' is higher in the image than the brick point, so it is farther.
